newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to consider support for Albania force.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to consider support for Albania force.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would not take part in a multinational force to protect aid deliveries in strife-torn Albania but would consider requests to support it.

State Department spokesman John Dinger also said the United States would take part in an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) civilian mission to Albania to support democracy and elections, expected in June.

Italy plans to lead a multinational force of about 2,500 troops or police, with another 2,500 in reserve, to protect deliveries of food and medicine in the former communist state which has been racked by armed unrest.
France, Spain, Portugal, Austria, Turkey, Greece and Romania have said they will take part in the force, which was approved last week by the United Nations Security Council.
"While the U.S. will not be a participant, we will consider specific requests for support for its efforts on a case-by-case basis," Dinger told a news briefing.
He refused to speculate on what sort of requests Washington might receive.
He said the United States "fully supports and will participate in" a planned OSCE mission in Albania to promote political reconciliation and democracy, as well as to aid humanitarian relief.
Much of southern Albania is in rebel hands after protests at the collapse of popular savings schemes this year spilled into insurrection.
